verdict_rationale: One CONFIRMED Important finding: fixing.md waiver-honoring is keyed only on the PR Test Plan, which on the /prflow:implement path is seeded at Phase 4.2 AFTER the Phase 3 fix loop runs, so the waiver is invisible to the fixer on the primary path (partially defeats AC4). fix_severity_threshold=suggestion, so this is actionable in the loop.
diff_scope: prose/config-only (8 markdown/skill/agent files + example config + changeset); no .py/.sh/.yml behavior code changed

cap_drops.reason: iterations=first-only override in live config; fix-loop iteration 3 (N>=2) -> excluded (correct, not a shortfall)
has_new_types=false (no types introduced; prose/config diff) -> applicability-gated out
test-relevance predicate did not match: no test file changed and every changed path has a config_only extension (.md/.json) -> applicability-gated out

phase3_findings.description: skills/review-and-fix/references/fixing.md keys waiver-honoring on 'when the PR's Test Plan records a waiver', but on the /prflow:implement path the Test Plan is seeded at Phase 4.2 AFTER the Phase 3 fix loop, so the waiver line does not yet exist when the fixer runs. Its sibling composition in phase-3-agents.md has a dual-source arm (workpad 'test-authoring-waiver:' notes on the implementing run; seeded Test Plan line on later reviews); fixing.md lacks it. The fixer has $ISSUE_NUMBER/workpad access on the implement path, so reading the workpad note is available. Consequence: the fixer's own test-first gate can re-impose waivable ceremony on waived surfaces during the implement fix loop, partially defeating AC4.
phase3_findings.remedy: Give fixing.md the same dual-source arm as phase-3-agents.md: on the implementing run read the workpad notes beginning 'test-authoring-waiver:'; on a later/standalone review read the seeded 'Test authoring waived:' Test Plan line.

phase3_findings.description: The §2.3 waiver --note mandates no internal separator ('naming what was waived and why'), but pr-description seeds 'Test authoring waived: <ceremony> — <reason>'. If the note lacks ' — ', the ceremony/reason split is cosmetic-only. Fails toward strictness (an unmatched surface just gets full review). Pinning the note grammar would make the producer/consumer contract exact.

The reviewer's cap precision rests entirely on how carefully the §2.3 note spells surface paths (free-text, unvalidated). Acceptable given the fail-closed default (an unmatched/vague surface gets full strictness). Awareness only.

Momentary band-labeling tension: honor rule uses sub-critical (1-7) vs 8-10 Critical Gaps, which matches the Output Format buckets, but the Rating Guidelines block groups '7-8: Important business logic', so a reader may briefly read 7 as adjacent to 8. Behavior-inert wording; not a falsehood (honor rule anchors on the unambiguous 'Critical Gaps bucket').

prior_findings_status.iter2_important_test_plan_producer: RESOLVED — pr-description Step 1 now derives TEST_AUTHORING_WAIVER_ITEMS from workpad notes beginning 'test-authoring-waiver:' and Step 2 seeds a re-derived 'Test authoring waived:' Test Plan line (symmetric to Post-Merge Verification); phase-2-sweeps-contract.md §2.3 mandates the stable marker; phase-3-agents.md names both the marker and the seeded line for the reviewer. Verified: workpad.py --note writes to ## Progress as '  - HH:MM:SS — <text>', matching the scan; 'test-authoring-waiver:' is not a reserved-marker prefix so the --note is not silently rejected.
prior_findings_status.iter1_suggestion_8_10_band: RESOLVED at 745fcaa93 — pr-test-analyzer honor rule now states 8-10 (Critical Gaps) stays at full severity; consistent with Output Format buckets and the changeset.

phase_4_1_report.actionable: Important: fixing.md dual-source waiver gap (defeats AC4 on the implement path).
